key_insight: Diffusion-DRF turns non-differentiable preference signals into a differentiable reward flow so reward gradients can backpropagate through video diffusion fine-tuning, enabling stable, end-to-end alignment between text prompts and generated video.
problem_solved: Current T2V fine-tuning relies on non-differentiable human or learned preference signals, which is label‑intensive, bias‑prone, vulnerable to reward hacking, and leads to unstable training.
method: Introduce a Differentiable Reward Flow (DRF) that converts preference signals into a gradient-friendly module that interfaces with the diffusion sampling/denoising pipeline.
Integrate DRF with a pretrained video diffusion model to enable end-to-end fine-tuning (reward gradients flow back into the generator) while preserving pretrained capabilities.
Train with a differentiable preference objective (DPO-compatible surrogate and regularization) to improve text alignment and visual fidelity while reducing label dependence and reward-hacking risk.
impact: Makes preference-based fine-tuning of video diffusion models more label-efficient, robust, and harder to game, giving practitioners a practical path to better text-to-video alignment and more stable training.
